lesson_title: The Earphone Knot: Why Poverty Won't Untangle
hook_text: Pull one wire and the knot tightens. That's why poverty is so hard to fix — and why one answer is always wrong.
clip_script: Why is poverty so stubborn? Because its causes arrive pre-tangled, like earphones pulled from a school bag. Tug one wire and the knot tightens somewhere else. Watch the knot close around one West Coast fishing family. The fish stocks thin out — that is the resource wire. The catch shrinks, so the eldest daughter leaves school to gut and pack at the harbour — the education wire pulls tight. The family sells whole fish cheaply, then buys tinned fish back at four times the price — the trade wire. No reliable electricity means no ice machine, no freezer, no selling on their own terms — the energy wire. And beneath everything, the family lives on this windblown edge because their grandparents were moved off the front-line fishing grounds by decree — the history wire, knotted through every other one. Here is the skill: never explain one wire on its own. Thin catches pull a child from school, no school pulls down wages, low wages pull the sea harder, and the stocks thin further. And one wire has a strange name — the resource curse. Angola has the oil and stays poor; Botswana took its diamonds and built schools. Never the rocks. Always what a country does with them.
visual_style: A pair of tangled earphones morphing into labelled wires — resources, education, trade, energy, history — each one tightening as it is named over scenes of a West Coast harbour; a final split screen of oil derricks against classrooms.
mood: Serious and gripping, ending with agency rather than despair.
pacing: Steady wire-by-wire build, tightening rhythm through the chain, clean landing on the resource-curse reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to untangle the knot in any essay.
